title: No Longer Allowed In Another World
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A parody isekai whose hero, 'Sensei', is modeled on novelist Osamu Dazai. About to complete a suicide pact with his lover Sacchan in 1948, he is hit by a truck and summoned to a fantasy world as a hero; he wants only to die, but keeps living to find Sacchan, who arrived as one of the evil 'Fallen Angels', and his power can send other summoned people home (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb; AniList).
life_message: Played as dark comedy: a man who wants only to die keeps helping others to live, though the story never fully rejects his wish.

content.note: Fantasy fights with evil Other Worlders (Wikipedia); not graphic as far as summaries show.
Harem setup and jealousy (AniList Female Harem; Wikipedia); fan service and a near-assault by a tentacle monster in the anime (Anime Feminist; manga to verify).
Constant painkiller and sleeping-pill use (Wikipedia; Anime Feminist); a leaf-smoking business in one arc (Wikipedia).
Suicidal ideation and a suicide pact drive the plot, often played for laughs (Wikipedia; AniList Suicide 91%; Anime Feminist on the anime).
Pills eaten as snacks and hanging attempts shown as comedy (Anime Feminist, anime; Wikipedia pills).

dominant: Absurdist dark comedy about despair; parody of isekai wish-fulfilment

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Religious Church shown as the schemer behind summonings (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Poetic death wish over survival (Seven Seas blurb).

folkways.japan: Osamu Dazai's novel No Longer Human and his 1948 death with a lover are canonical in Japanese literature, and the series parodies both, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: Anime Feminist (anime) finds no clear point beyond the repeated death-wish joke; Wikipedia shows episodic lessons.

personified.ideology: Religious authority summoning heroes for its own ends

delivery.note: The comedy treats both Sensei's despair and others' heroics with irony rather than arguing for one side.

winners_losers: Sensei keeps surviving and sends troubled Other Worlders home; summoners and power-abusers lose. Sympathy goes to the despairing outsider.
to_verify: Anime Feminist review covers the anime, not the manga; fan service and tentacle scene may differ in the manga
